/-!
# Erdős Problem 645

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/645](https://www.erdosproblems.com/645)
- [BrLa99] Brown, Tom C. and Landman, Bruce M., Monochromatic arithmetic progressions with large
  differences. Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. (1999), 21--35.
-/


namespace Erdos645

/--
If ℕ is $2$-coloured then there must exist a monochromatic three-term arithmetic progression
$x,x+d,x+2d$ such that $d>x$.

This was first proved by Brown and Landman [BrLa99], who in fact show that this is always possible
with $d>f(x)$ for any increasing function $f$.

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle and ChatGPT.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos645.lean"]
theorem erdos_645 (c : ℕ → Bool) : ∃ x d, 0 < x ∧ x < d ∧
    (∃ C, c x = C ∧ c (x + d) = C ∧ c (x + 2 * d) = C) := by
  sorry

end Erdos645

reformulations.difference: Lean colors all natural numbers, including zero, but explicitly requires a positive first term. Brown–Landman work with positive integers; the problem page simply writes ℕ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Restriction to positive integers and arbitrary extension at zero give equivalent coloring assertions, since every queried term is positive. Even if the page's ℕ allows a witness x=0, positivity does not strengthen the universal assertion: apply that assertion to n ↦ c(2n+1), then transform a witness (x,d) into (2x+1,2d). Since d>x, the transformed difference exceeds its positive first term. Both equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the admitted problem theorem.
